meta.note: Exam-style written questions. Chapter 6 has 3 MCQs (Stage 2) and 9 long-form exercises here.

questions.question: What is the function of receptors in our body? Think of situations where receptors do not work properly. What problems are likely to arise?
hints: Receptors detect stimuli at dendritic tips in sense organs.
Examples: gustatory (taste), olfactory (smell), photoreceptors (light).
If receptors fail: blindness, deafness, loss of taste.
questions.model_answer:
**Function:** Receptors are specialised tips of nerve cells in sense organs that **detect environmental stimuli** and trigger nerve impulses.

**Examples:** Gustatory receptors (taste), olfactory receptors (smell), receptors in eye and ear.

**If receptors fail:** Cannot detect changes — **blindness** (no light detection), **deafness** (no sound), **loss of taste/smell** — so the body cannot respond appropriately.
marking_points: Gives examples of receptors or sense organs
common_mistakes: Not giving examples of receptor failure

questions.question: Draw the structure of a neuron and explain its function.
hints: Label dendrites, cell body, axon, axon terminals.
Dendrites receive; axon transmits impulse.
Synapse at end connects to next neuron or effector.
questions.model_answer:
**Structure:** Dendrites (receive signals) → cell body (contains nucleus) → axon (long fibre) → axon terminals (synapse with next cell).

**Function:** Neuron **acquires information** at dendrites, creates **electrical impulse** that travels along axon, and passes signal via **synapse** to next neuron, muscle, or gland.
marking_points: Correct diagram with dendrites, cell body, axon labelled
Explains transmission along axon and synapse
common_mistakes: Labelling synapse as part of the neuron itself

questions.question: How does phototropism occur in plants?
hints: Auxin synthesised at shoot tip.
Light from one side → auxin diffuses to shady side.
Shady side cells elongate more → shoot bends toward light.
questions.model_answer: When light comes from one direction, **auxin** (plant hormone) at the shoot tip **diffuses to the shady side**. Higher auxin concentration on the shady side causes those cells to **grow longer**, making the shoot **bend toward light** — this is positive phototropism.
marking_points: Uneven auxin distribution toward shady side
common_mistakes: Saying plants move like animals using muscles

questions.question: Which signals will get disrupted in case of a spinal cord injury?
hints: Spinal cord connects brain to rest of body.
Carries sensory signals up and motor signals down.
Reflex arcs also processed in spinal cord.
questions.model_answer: Spinal cord injury disrupts **communication between brain and body parts below the injury**. **Sensory signals** from body to brain and **motor signals** from brain to muscles are blocked. **Reflex actions** below the injury site may also be lost.
marking_points: Mentions loss of sensation or paralysis below injury
common_mistakes: Confusing spinal cord with vertebral column only

questions.question: How does chemical coordination occur in plants?
hints: Plants use hormones (phytohormones).
Synthesised in one part, diffuse to action site.
Examples: auxin, gibberellin, cytokinin, abscisic acid.
questions.model_answer: Plants use **plant hormones** (e.g. auxin, gibberellin, cytokinin) that are **produced in one part** and **diffuse** to cells where they act. They regulate **growth, cell division, and responses** to light, gravity, and water — without a nervous system.
marking_points: Produced at one site, act elsewhere
Names at least one hormone with function

questions.question: What is the need for a system of control and coordination in an organism?
hints: Organisms face changing environments.
Must detect stimuli and respond appropriately.
Multicellular bodies need communication between parts.
questions.model_answer: Organisms constantly face **changes in their environment**. They must **detect stimuli** and produce **appropriate, timely responses** for survival. In multicellular organisms, different parts must **work together** — control and coordination systems (nervous and hormonal) ensure the correct response reaches the right body part.

questions.question: How are involuntary actions and reflex actions different from each other?
hints: Reflex: sudden, specific stimulus, via reflex arc.
Involuntary: continuous, no specific trigger (heartbeat).
Both lack conscious control.
questions.model_answer:
**Reflex actions:** sudden, in response to a **specific stimulus**, via **reflex arc** in spinal cord (e.g. hand withdrawal from flame).

**Involuntary actions:** **no specific stimulus** needed, controlled by mid-brain/hind-brain, run continuously (e.g. heartbeat, digestion, salivation).

Both lack conscious control, but reflex needs a trigger; involuntary does not.
common_mistakes: Saying all involuntary actions are reflexes
Claiming reflex actions involve conscious thought

questions.question: Compare and contrast nervous and hormonal mechanisms for control and coordination in animals.
hints: Nervous: electrical impulses, fast, through nerves.
Hormonal: chemicals in blood, slow, widespread.
Give at least three differences.
questions.model_answer:
| Feature | Nervous | Hormonal |
|---|---|---|
| Signal | Electrical impulse | Chemical hormone |
| Speed | Very fast (ms) | Slower (minutes) |
| Pathway | Nerve fibres | Bloodstream |
| Duration | Short-lived | Longer lasting |
| Reach | Connected cells only | All cells with receptors |
common_mistakes: Saying hormones use nerves to travel

questions.question: What is the difference between the manner in which movement takes place in a sensitive plant and the movement in our legs?
hints: Mimosa: turgor change, fast, no growth, no muscles.
Legs: muscle contraction, nervous control, voluntary.
Compare mechanism, speed, and tissues involved.
questions.model_answer:
**Sensitive plant (Mimosa):** movement by **change in water content** (turgor) in cells — **no muscles, no nerves**, very **fast**, **no growth** involved.

**Leg movement:** **muscle contraction** controlled by **nervous system** — can be **voluntary** (walking) or involuntary; uses specialised muscle proteins.
marking_points: Legs: muscle contraction with nervous control
common_mistakes: Saying Mimosa uses auxin for folding
